bullets: How to add fractions whose pieces are not the same size
slides.heading: Adding fractions: 1/2 + 1/4
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we are going to add one half and one quarter, and by the end you will be able to explain exactly why the answer is three quarters.

bullets: Convert halves into quarters so every piece is the same size
Add fractions with the same bottom number and explain why the bottom number stays
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud slowly and tell the class: keep these in mind, because our exit ticket at the end will ask you to do exactly these two things.

bullets: You eat half a pizza at lunch, then a quarter of the same pizza after school
How much pizza did you eat altogether - and why is the answer not two sixths?
slides.heading: Half a pizza, then a quarter more
slides.notes: Ask for a show of hands and take two or three guesses without judging them yet; say: hold on to your idea, because the size of the pieces is the key to the whole lesson.

bullets: The bottom number, the denominator, names the piece size: halves are bigger pieces than quarters
Fractions can only be added directly when their pieces are the same size
Changing 1/2 into 2/4 changes the pieces, never the amount
slides.heading: Same-size pieces can be added
slides.notes: Say this part slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: the denominator is not a number to add - it names how big each piece is, and pieces must match before we count them.

bullets: One bar shows 1/2 shaded blue and another shows 1/4 shaded green
A quarter fits inside a half exactly twice
slides.heading: Adding fractions
slides.notes: Point at the animation and narrate what is happening: watch how the green quarter slides into the blue half - it fits exactly twice, and that fit is what lets us convert.

bullets: Split the half into two quarters: 1/2 = 2/4
Now every piece in the sum is a quarter
slides.heading: Make the pieces the same size
slides.notes: Tell them to watch the blade cut the half in two: nothing was added or taken away, the same amount is just wearing smaller pieces, so now both fractions speak quarters.

bullets: Count the quarters: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4
The bottom number stays 4 because the piece size never changed
slides.heading: Count the quarters
slides.notes: Count the three quarter pieces aloud with the class, one, two, three quarters; say: we added the tops because they count the pieces, and the bottom stayed 4 because the pieces stayed quarters.

bullets: Tempting wrong turn: Adding tops and bottoms: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/6.
The bottom number names the piece size, so it cannot be added like the tops
slides.heading: Watch out: 1/2 + 1/4 is not 2/6
slides.notes: Name the trap out loud before anyone falls into it: adding the bottoms pretends the pieces changed size into sixths, but no sixth was ever cut - the pieces stayed quarters all along.

bullets: Step 1: convert the half into quarters, 1/2 = 2/4
Step 2: add the tops and keep the bottom, 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4
slides.heading: Worked example: 1/2 + 1/4
slides.notes: Talk through the two steps slowly and name each one as you write it; say: notice the amount never changed in step 1, we only re-cut the same half into smaller pieces.

bullets: Work out 1/2 + 1/4 with the bar cards: convert first, then count the quarters
Careful - a classmate writes Adding tops and bottoms: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/6. Explain to them why that is wrong
slides.heading: Your turn: convert, then count
slides.notes: Give pairs two minutes with the bar cards, then cold-call one pair and press them on the trap: if the bottoms really added, what size would the pieces be, and did anyone ever cut sixths?

bullets: Write out 1/2 + 1/4 in two steps and give the answer
Finish this sentence and defend it: 1/2 + 1/4 is not 2/6, because ...
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the words piece size in your last answer - if you can explain why the bottom number cannot be added, you have cracked today's lesson.
